regime.summary: Market-wide mood is extreme fear: Fear & Greed is 10.0 today, down from 28.0-32.0 a week ago and 13.0 yesterday (news.json fear_greed), echoed by uniformly negative RSS tone on BTC/ETH/XRP (ETF-outflow and 'worst asset' headlines) while BTC/ETH/SOL/XRP all sit in xs.json's R9 (liquidation) cell with funding at the bottom of their 90d range (p0-p4). The sentiment panel itself is brand new (collecting since 16:21Z, ~1h of history, 0h baseline), so every ticker's trend is 'insufficient' - this is a snapshot of raw headline tone on 1-7 items per ticker, not a measured spike, and web search is used below only to sanity-check direction, not to add a number the panel can't yet support.

ideas.thesis: Mood is at a fresh extreme (F&G 10.0, down from 28-32 a week ago) and all four majors sit in R9 (liquidation); RSS tone on BTC/ETH/XRP is uniformly negative, matching the ETF-outflow headlines. But the sentiment panel has 0h baseline (collecting since 16:21Z) and only 1-7 headlines per ticker, so this confirms the mood the tape already shows rather than adding anything new.

evidence.note: cointelegraph, decrypt, bitcoinist, forklog, bravenewcoin, sentimentrader, kucoin, mexc each ran an 'extreme fear / capitulation' piece in this window

invalidation.condition: F&G closes back above 30 and BTC headline tone turns net positive (>= +0.2 avg over >= 10 headlines) while sentiment collection keeps running uninterrupted

ideas.reasoning: Ranked first: the best-evidenced read available right now (F&G and regime cells are both snapshot facts), but it is confirmation of the tape, not an independent signal - R-NEWS-7 found attention/F&G did not predict BTC direction or vol.

ideas.thesis: SOL funding is at the bottom of its 90d range (p0, -21.3% ann.), the most stressed of the four majors, yet attention is near zero (1 headline, tone 0.00). Web coverage frames SOL as the one major with net ETF inflows (~$269M cumulative) against that funding stress - a quiet divergence to flag, not trade: H-SENT1 is untested, sample too small to size on.

evidence.note: nexo.com Dispatch #269 (ETH & SOL): SOL spot ETFs ~$269M cumulative inflows, contrasted with BTC/ETH ETF outflows this month

invalidation.condition: SOL mentions_24h rises past 10 with trend no longer 'insufficient' while funding normalizes back above its 20th percentile

ideas.reasoning: Second: a genuine attention-vs-positioning gap (the 'quiet asset' pattern in the agent brief), capped by the tiny sample and SOL's own insufficient trend; R-AVOID-1 means the low funding percentile alone is not a reason to act.

ideas.thesis: ETH's tone_24h (-0.74) is the most negative in the panel, but it rests on one headline ('worst asset of all time') - n=1, lexicon noise, not a measured shift. Web search shows ETH ETFs in their worst monthly outflow (~$728.6M weekly, third-highest on record); if the RSS sample grows and stays this negative it would agree with that real number - right now it is one headline next to it.

evidence.note: coverage of Blockworks/Sherwood ETF-flow data: spot ETH ETFs' third-highest weekly outflow since inception, worst month on record

invalidation.condition: ETH news_24h sample grows to >= 5 headlines while average tone stays <= -0.5, i.e. the reading survives a larger sample

ideas.reasoning: Third and lowest conviction: a sanity check on whether the news agent's tone read on ETH is a real shift or a 1-headline artefact; not a standalone call either way.

data_gaps: Reddit keys missing (REDDIT_CLIENT_ID / REDDIT_CLIENT_SECRET / REDDIT_USER_AGENT); 0 of 147 collected items are Reddit - the panel is RSS headlines only, no comment/post-level data.

Collection started 2026-11-15T16:21:37Z, under an hour before this cycle; baseline_hours = 0 for every ticker, so z_mentions/z_tone/trend are 'insufficient' across the whole panel - nothing here is a measured rise or fall yet.

sentiment.json mentions_24h undercounts against news.json's fuller 24h RSS tally (e.g. SOL 1 vs 4, BTC 7 vs 48) because the sentiment collector's own window is only ~1h old; news.json counts_24h.by_ticker is the better 24h reference until the sentiment panel catches up.

Web search results for this 48h window were internally inconsistent on exact index values and BTC price levels across different outlets (Fear & Greed cited variously as 10 / 14 / 15 / 5; BTC price cited near $63k / $73k / $83k / $94k / $98k, some apparently from outside this window). Only the shared qualitative direction (extreme fear, persistent ETF outflows) is used above; no single external number is treated as fact.
No raw Reddit thread content was available; web search surfaced only secondary coverage of Reddit/X mood (via Santiment/Cointelegraph), not primary threads.

honesty.base_rate: No idea above proposes a direction. Absent an edge, a random entry has roughly 50/50 odds of hitting target before stop within a horizon (R-BUDGET-1); H-SENT1 (sentiment as a decision input) is proposed but untested, so it carries no weight on its own.
conflicts: R-NEWS-7: headline tone and Fear & Greed did not predict BTC direction or vol in prior tests.
R-AVOID-1: funding-contrarian ('crowd is short/long so fade it') failed; SOL's low funding percentile alone is not a reason to act.
R-BUDGET-1: stacking sentiment on top of xs/news does not make direction more predictable.
Every ticker's trend is 'insufficient' (baseline_hours = 0); none of this is a confirmed spike, only a single snapshot.
honesty.what_would_change_my_mind: Reddit keys provisioned and at least 24h (ideally the 60 days H-SENT1 needs) of continuous collection giving real z_mentions/z_tone, with a genuine spike that either agrees or cleanly disagrees with the same-day funding/OI/price move.
